newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar slips to another 8-year low close.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar slips to another 8-year low close.

text.p: Heavy commercial demand for the U.S. dollar on Tuesday triggered greenback buying and sank the Taiwan dollar to a new eight-year low close for the second consecutive day, dealers said.
The local unit dived to as low as T$27.928 before recovering somewhat, but still ended at an eight-year low of T$27.917, weakened from Monday's T$27.908 finish.
Tuesday's closing marked the lowest level since a T$28.03 finish on January 7, 1989.
Tunrover through dealers was US$277 million.
Dealers said the psychological T$28 level loomed in view.

The Taiwan dollar was slowly testing its downside, they said, due to importers' quarter-end U.S. dollar demand and strong expectations that the local unit would slip after the central bank on Monday abandoned its defence at T$27.90.
"The Taiwan dollar is definitely in a downtrend," said one dealer. "You can tell the central bank is quietly smoothing the Taiwan dollar's fall, but its action is not that aggressive."
"Had the central bank not intervened, the Taiwan dollar soon would have fallen to T$28," he added.

Some dealers said they suspected the central bank may orchestrate "political intervention" to bolster the currency ahead of Hong Kong's July 1 handover by Britain to China, a sensitive issue for Taiwan as it is seen by Beijing as a wayward province that also must be "reunified with the motherland".
Market factors could give the central bank some cover.

"Seasonal U.S. dollar demand should gradually fade by the end of June," the dealer said. "At that time, the central bank may try to support the Taiwan dollar, giving other people a good impression about Taiwan's financial stability."
A June depreciation was in line with the average forecast of six senior Taipei dealers in an informal May 30 Reuters Poll.

Four of the dealers said Taiwan's easing dollar would break eight-year support at T$28 in the third quarter, citing slack economic growth and political uncertainties -- but not before the central bank put up a strong defence to slow the slide.
Two dissenting dealers acknowledged the depreciation pressure, but said the central bank would mount a defence of such vigour that the currency would remain above T$28.
